fullPassage:
What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.

Jason: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said "Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job." It felt great to help save someone's life!

Olivia: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me from running again. Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.

Yuna: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough courage. Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.

questions.passage: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I (A)[immediately / hesitantly] called 911 and explained the (B)[situation / decoration]. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the (C)[paramedics / pedestrians] arrived.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 즉시(immediately) 911에 전화해서 상황(situation)을 설명했고, 구급대원(paramedics)이 올 때까지 CPR을 수행했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① immediately — situation — paramedics: 원문 일치
❌ ② hesitantly(망설이며): immediately의 반의어
❌ ③ decoration(장식): situation과 무관
❌ ④ pedestrians(보행자): paramedics와 전혀 다른 의미
det.tip: immediately(즉시) ↔ hesitantly(망설이며), paramedics(구급대원) ↔ pedestrians(보행자)

questions.passage: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a (A)[sudden / gradual] end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not (B)[hopeful / hopeless]. The doctors said my knee injury would (C)[prevent / encourage] me from running again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 올림픽 꿈이 갑자기(sudden) 끝났고, 검사 결과가 희망적이지 않았으며(not hopeful), 부상이 달리기를 막을(prevent) 것이라고 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ sudden — hopeful — prevent: 원문 일치. not hopeful이 문맥에 맞음
❌ ① gradual(점진적인): 원문은 sudden(갑작스러운)
❌ ② hopeless: not hopeful ≠ hopeless. 원문은 'not hopeful'
❌ ④ encourage(격려하다): prevent의 반의어
det.tip: not hopeful(희망적이지 않은) ≠ hopeless(절망적인). 부정어 not + 긍정형용사 구조에 주의!

questions.passage: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to (A)[inspire / discourage] and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the (B)[annual / occasional] speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough (C)[courage / cowardice].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 청중에게 영감(inspire)을 주고 싶었지만, 매년 열리는(annual) 대회에 나갈 용기(courage)가 없었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② inspire — annual — courage: 원문 일치
❌ ① discourage(낙담시키다): inspire의 반의어
❌ ③ occasional(가끔의): annual의 반의어
❌ ④ cowardice(비겁함): courage의 반의어
det.tip: inspire(영감을 주다) ↔ discourage(낙담시키다), annual(매년의) ↔ occasional(가끔의), courage(용기) ↔ cowardice(비겁함)

questions.passage: I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the <u>① situation</u>. Luckily, the clerk regained <u>② consciousness</u>. After putting the clerk in the <u>③ ambulance</u>, the paramedics said "Thank you for being <u>④ cowardly</u>. You did a wonderful job."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '용감한(brave)'인데, '비겁한(cowardly)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① situation: 상황, 원문 일치
✅ ② consciousness: 의식, 원문 일치
✅ ③ ambulance: 구급차, 원문 일치
❌ ④ cowardly(비겁한) → brave(용감한): 반의어로 교체됨
det.tip: brave(용감한) ↔ cowardly(비겁한). 구급대원이 Jason에게 '용감했다'고 감사를 표한 장면.

questions.passage: Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too <u>① painful</u>. So I shut out everything <u>② related</u> to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my <u>③ extraordinary</u> high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called <u>④ sports medicine</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 '평범한(ordinary)' 고등학교 생활인데, '특별한(extraordinary)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① painful: 고통스러운, 원문 일치
✅ ② related: 관련된, 원문 일치
❌ ③ extraordinary(특별한) → ordinary(평범한): 반의어로 교체됨
✅ ④ sports medicine: 스포츠 의학, 원문 일치
det.tip: ordinary(평범한) ↔ extraordinary(특별한). 스포츠 없는 '평범한' 고등학교 생활에 적응하려 했다.

questions.passage: This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my <u>① brave</u> decision, I am studying to be a star on the <u>② sidelines</u> instead of on the playing field. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get <u>③ confident</u>. I didn't want to make a <u>④ fool</u> of myself.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문은 사람들 앞에서 말할 기회가 오면 '겁이 났다(scared)'인데, '자신감 있는(confident)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① brave: 용감한, 원문 일치
✅ ② sidelines: 사이드라인, 원문 일치
❌ ③ confident(자신감 있는) → scared(겁난): 반의어로 교체됨
✅ ④ fool: 바보, 원문 일치 (make a fool of myself)
det.tip: scared(겁난) ↔ confident(자신감 있는). Yuna는 사람들 앞에서 말하는 것이 두려웠다.

questions.passage: What does it mean to be brave? There is no single __________, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 용감하다는 것이 무엇을 의미하는지 하나의 정의(definition)는 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② definition: 정의, 원문 일치 — 용감함의 단일 정의가 없다는 맥락
❌ ① direction: 방향, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ decision: 결정, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ destination: 목적지, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: definition(정의) — 'What does it mean'이 단서. 의미/정의를 묻는 맥락.

questions.passage: It deals with the treatment and __________ of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 스포츠 의학은 스포츠 부상의 치료와 예방(prevention)을 다룬다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ prevention: 예방, 원문 일치 — treatment and prevention 쌍
❌ ① promotion: 홍보/승진, 문맥 부적절
❌ ② production: 생산, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ protection: 보호, 유사하지만 원문 불일치
det.tip: treatment(치료) and prevention(예방) — 의학 분야의 전형적 쌍. prevention ≠ protection.

questions.passage: I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a __________ lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나의 용기 있는 행동은 나에게 귀중한(valuable) 교훈을 가르쳐주었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① valuable: 귀중한, 원문 일치 — 용기를 통해 배운 소중한 교훈
❌ ② trivial: 사소한, 반의어
❌ ③ painful: 고통스러운, 문맥 부적절 (긍정적 결론)
❌ ④ complicated: 복잡한, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: valuable(귀중한) — 'I can do anything that I put my mind to'라는 긍정적 교훈의 수식어.

questions.passage: I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to <u>perform</u> CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 perform과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 교환원이 구급대원이 올 때까지 점원에게 CPR을 수행(perform)하라고 요청했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② carry out: 수행하다, perform의 동의어
❌ ① cancel: 취소하다, 반의어
❌ ③ postpone: 연기하다, 다른 의미
❌ ④ avoid: 피하다, 반의어
det.tip: perform = carry out = conduct: 수행하다, 실행하다.

questions.passage: Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I <u>came across</u> an interesting university major called sports medicine.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 came across와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 어느 날 스포츠 의학이라는 흥미로운 대학 전공을 우연히 발견(came across)했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ ran into: 우연히 마주치다, came across의 동의어
❌ ① searched for: 찾아다녔다, 의도적 행동
❌ ② gave up: 포기했다, 다른 의미
❌ ④ looked after: 돌보았다, 다른 의미
det.tip: came across = ran into = stumbled upon: 우연히 발견하다/마주치다.

questions.passage: So I <u>made up my mind</u> and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 made up my mind와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 마음을 굳히고(made up my mind) 이 전공에 지원했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ decided: 결심했다, made up my mind의 동의어
❌ ① changed my opinion: 의견을 바꿨다, 다른 의미
❌ ② lost my temper: 화를 냈다, 다른 의미
❌ ③ came to my senses: 정신을 차렸다, 유사하나 다른 의미
det.tip: make up one's mind = decide: 결심하다, 마음을 정하다.

questions.passage: The doctors said my knee injury would <u>prevent</u> me from running again. Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 prevent와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: 무릎 부상이 다시 뛰는 것을 막을(prevent) 것이라고 의사가 말했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① allow: 허락하다, prevent의 반의어
❌ ② block: 차단하다, 동의어
❌ ③ hinder: 방해하다, 동의어
❌ ④ prohibit: 금지하다, 동의어
det.tip: prevent(막다) ↔ allow(허락하다). block, hinder, prohibit은 모두 '막다/방해하다' 계열.

questions.passage: I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get <u>scared</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 scared와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: 사람들 앞에서 말할 기회가 올 때마다 겁이 났다(scared).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ confident: 자신감 있는, scared의 반의어
❌ ① frightened: 겁먹은, 동의어
❌ ② terrified: 무서워하는, 동의어
❌ ③ anxious: 불안한, 유사어
det.tip: scared(겁난) ↔ confident(자신감 있는). frightened, terrified, anxious는 모두 '두려움' 계열.

questions.passage: I was about to take the <u>lead</u> in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 lead와 같은 의미로 사용된 것은?
ch: Lead is a heavy metal used in batteries.
This road will lead you to the station.
She took the lead in the final lap of the marathon.
He is the lead actor in the school play.

det.korean: 경주에서 선두(lead)를 잡으려던 순간 무릎에 통증을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ took the lead: 선두를 잡다 (본문과 같은 의미)
❌ ① Lead(납): 금속 이름
❌ ② lead you to: 이끌다/안내하다 (동사)
❌ ④ lead actor: 주연의 (형용사)
det.tip: lead: ① 납(금속) ② 이끌다(동사) ③ 선두/리드(명사) ④ 주연의(형용사). 본문은 ③.

questions.passage: I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech <u>contest</u> at my school.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 contest와 같은 의미로 사용된 것은?
ch: The lawyers plan to contest the decision in court.
She won first place in the national writing contest.
Several parties will contest the election next month.
I don't contest the fact that changes are needed.

det.korean: 매년 열리는 학교 연설 대회(contest)에 참가하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② writing contest: 글쓰기 대회 (본문과 같은 의미 — 명사, 대회)
❌ ① contest the decision: 이의를 제기하다 (동사)
❌ ③ contest the election: 선거에 출마하다 (동사)
❌ ④ don't contest: 이의를 제기하지 않다 (동사)
det.tip: contest: ① 대회/경연(명사) ② 이의를 제기하다/다투다(동사). 본문은 ①.

questions.passage: I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. __________
questions.stem: 다음 중 영어 표현과 한국어 뜻이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

det.korean: immediately = 즉시.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ immediately = 즉시: 올바른 짝
❌ ① consciousness = 의식 (편리함 = convenience)
❌ ② paramedics = 구급대원 (보행자 = pedestrians)
❌ ③ ambulance = 구급차 (응급실 = emergency room)
det.tip: consciousness(의식), paramedics(구급대원), ambulance(구급차), immediately(즉시)

questions.passage: It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. __________
questions.stem: 다음 중 영어 표현과 한국어 뜻이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

det.korean: prevention = 예방.
det.analysis:
✅ ① prevention = 예방: 올바른 짝
❌ ② treatment = 치료 (대우도 가능하나 본문 맥락은 '치료')
❌ ③ injury = 부상 (주사 = injection)
❌ ④ ordinary = 평범한 (특별한 = extraordinary)
det.tip: prevention(예방), treatment(치료), injury(부상), ordinary(평범한)

questions.passage: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter __________ race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end.
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태를 고르시오.

champion

det.korean: 전국 100미터 선수권(championship) 대회에서 올림픽 꿈이 갑작스럽게 끝났다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ championship: 선수권 대회, 명사로 race를 수식
❌ ① champion: 우승자, 문법적 가능하나 원문은 championship
❌ ② championed: 과거분사, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ championing: 현재분사, 문맥 부적절
det.tip: champion(우승자) → championship(선수권 대회). championship race = 선수권 경주.

questions.passage: But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to. Last year, however, was my final chance before __________ from high school.
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태를 고르시오.

graduate

det.korean: 고등학교를 졸업하기(graduating) 전 마지막 기회였다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② graduating: 동명사, 전치사 before 뒤에 동명사 필요
